attribution.note: These are Marcus's own words, in the first person, in his own Substack post. He borrows the AGI definition from Klein's guest but endorses it as reasonable.

semantics.note: The normalised wording keeps 'almost zero chance', the borrowed AGI definition and the two-to-three-year window. The GPT-4.5 remark is a reason he gives, not a condition. It is about the future, but it is stated as a probability rather than a firm 'will not'.

contract.note: The contract correctly treats this as a probability judgement that the policy excludes from scoring. Recasting it as a flat prediction of no AGI would add to what Marcus said. The window ends 2028-03-05.

reviews.rationale: Not scored: Marcus gave a probability ('almost zero chance'), not a firm prediction. Under policy, probability statements are not_adjudicable, because one outcome cannot show whether a stated probability was right. Even if it were scored, the window runs to 2028-03-05, after the 2026-10-28 evaluation date, so it would not yet be due. The evidence packet is empty and no outcome search was run.
